attribution_finding: Murdock majority and Cohen majority; Murdock's second sentence is a rewritten summary rather than verbatim majority wording.
fidelity_finding: Murdock actually refers to constitutional liberties of press and religion and inevitably suppressing their exercise. Submitted sentence narrows/changes that wording. Cohen quoted fragments correspond with disclosed ellipsis/bracket.
pinpoint_finding: Murdock charge-for-enjoyment at113 (not114–115); tax restraint at114. Cohen25 correct.
scope_and_cutoff_finding: Murdock concerns flat license tax on religious evangelism, distinguishes ordinary property/income taxation and nominal regulatory fees. Do not broaden to immunity from every tax or fee. Cohen concerns offensiveness, not all exceptions to speech protection.
proposed_action_not_applied: Quote Murdock accurately or label paraphrase; change pinpoint to113–114.
prior_repair_status: No repair performed in this audit

ledger_excerpt:
From Murdock v. Pennsylvania, 319 U.S. 105, 114–115 (1943):
"A state may not impose a charge for the enjoyment of a right granted by the federal Constitution... The flat license tax here involved restrains in advance the freedom of the press and tends to suppress its exercise."
From Cohen v. California, 403 U.S. 15, 25 (1971):
"Surely the State has no right to cleanse public debate to the point where it is grammatically palatable to the most squeamish among us... [O]ne man's vulgarity is another's lyric."
